messages:
jess: Heads up — eu-central proxy cluster degraded ~10:15 UTC, hitting 503s for long-poll endpoints. Not an app deploy. Seeing lots of replica churn in the gpu-pool.

mike: Looking now. autoscaler logs show repeated scale-down/scale-up cycles for nodepool-gpu-euc1 over the last 6m. scale decisions triggered by podready=false probes.

arjun: Can you paste the probe failures? wondering if it's healthcheck timeout or kubelet eviction.

jess: Log snippet from the control plane:
```
2026-03-18T10:16:02Z autoscaler: scale_down: node node-gi-42 reason=low-util target=0.3->0.1
2026-03-18T10:16:06Z proxy: 503 GET /v1/stream id=abc user=svc-ingest region=euc1
2026-03-18T10:16:14Z autoscaler: scale_up: node node-gi-43 reason=pending-pods count=7
2026-03-18T10:16:21Z kubelet: eviction: "memory_pressure"
```

lina: kubelet eviction suggests OOMs on the nodes — but the pattern is weird because evictions coincide with proxy 503s. Might be network partition to metadata service or cgroup limits?

mike: Networking team: any known fabric maintenance in euc1?

ryan: Not scheduled. But noticed a flapping route on the regional proxy LB (infra-proxy-euc1) around 10:14-10:18 UTC. It returned to healthy after ~4m. Could explain in-flight requests failing and pods marking backend unhealthy.

arjun: That would trigger the autoscaler: probes fail -> pods not ready -> consolidate -> pending pods -> scale up -> repeat. We effectively created a feedback loop.

jess: Ops-bot shows traffic spike from a customer job at 10:13: single tenant burst bumped qps x6. Combined with short LB outage = cascading churn.

mike: Suggested immediate mitigation: 1) pause autoscaler for nodepool-gpu-euc1 (set cooldown and min replicas to current) 2) move heavy batch jobs to secondary region manually 3) increase probe timeouts for proxy endpoints short-term. Thoughts?

lina: +1 to pause autoscaler. Also recommend draining any nodes that show repeated OOMs and cordon them. We'll open a ticket to run node health diagnostics.

ryan: Implementing pause on autoscaler now: `kubectl annotate hpa gpu-pool -n infra autoscaler.paused=true --overwrite` (doing via runbook).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: annotation applied to hpa/gpu-pool in infra namespace by ryan.

jess: Good. I'm shifting canary traffic away from euc1 for r/w routes to eu-west fallback via routing policy. Doing it incrementally to avoid overwhelming west.

arjun: Also capturing metric artifact: prefix cache hit dropped during 10:12-10:18 window. Could be clients retrying and filling KV caches causing memory spikes -> kubelet evictions. Please preserve cache logs.

mike: After autoscaler pause, we see node churn stop and 503s reduce. Still watching for residual OOMs. Cost note: manual region failover will raise egress and inference unit costs — flagging to finance channel if we keep this >2h.

lina: Creating incident ticket with timeline + affected customers. Assigning follow-ups: networking to root cause LB flapping, infra to audit node kernel dmesg, platform to adjust short-term probes and run traffic shaping.

jess: Thanks. If networking confirms no infra change, next step is vendor escalations for LB hardware.

ryan: I'll leave autoscaler paused and post back when safe to unpause (recommend min-replicas=3 until we validate).

mike: Solid. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
